## Summary

Brings `dev/mi455x_v2` to `main`. Only `examples/` changes:

- Llama-3.1-8B pretraining on MI455X (#1288): `examples/megatron/models/llama3.1-8b/` (launcher, README) and
  `examples/megatron/configs/MI455X/llama3.1_8B-BF16-pretrain.yaml`. Attention runs on Primus-Turbo's FlyDSL
  kernels (AMD-AGI/Primus-Turbo#574, below).
- hipBLASLt tuning files for GPT-OSS 20B / 120B (#1296), and for the DeepSeek-V3 proxy and Llama-3.1-8B (#1295).
  Each launcher loads its file by default; `HIPBLASLT_TUNING_OVERRIDE_FILE=` restores hipBLASLt's own choice.

`main` (64fef81e) is merged in without conflicts. Of its changes, only #1286 (`te_ce_overwrite_input`) is on
these examples' path, and it is a no-op with the default image's TE (`parallel_cross_entropy` has no
`overwrite_input`).

## Primus-Turbo

The Primus-Turbo side is its `dev/mi455x_v2` branch (e3c6f03d): `main` ca1fdd67 plus

| PR | Change | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AMD-AGI/Primus-Turbo#574 | gfx1250 FlyDSL flash attention, head dim 128 | Llama-3.1-8B attention |
| AMD-AGI/Primus-Turbo#560 | gfx1250 FlyDSL sparse-MLA forward / backward (DeepSeek-V4) | none of these examples |

Llama-3.1-8B needs a checkout of it built in place as `TURBO_DIR` (see its README); AMD-AGI/Primus-Turbo#580
brings the branch to Primus-Turbo `main`. The DeepSeek-V3 proxy and GPT-OSS run on the image's Primus-Turbo
(`main` 21588d59).

## Results

This branch (d1144a89) on one node of 4x MI455X, `amdprimus/amdprimus:tas-20261019`, launcher defaults. ms/iter is
the average of iterations 3-10, mean of 3 runs per row that alternated between the rows of a table. DeepSeek-V3
and GPT-OSS on the image's Primus-Turbo, Llama-3.1-8B on Primus-Turbo `dev/mi455x_v2` (e3c6f03d).

| Example | Baseline | + FlyDSL | + hipBLASLt tuning (default) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DeepSeek-V3 proxy (EP4, 128 experts) | 2143 | 1159 (1.85x) | **1099 (1.95x)** |
| Llama-3.1-8B (DP4) | 1946 | 1137 (1.71x) | **1047 (1.86x)** |

Baseline: TE unfused attention and Triton grouped GEMM (DeepSeek-V3), Primus-Turbo Triton attention (Llama).

GPT-OSS (EP4, MBS 8 / GBS 64):

| Model | hipBLASLt default | + hipBLASLt tuning (default) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GPT-OSS 20B | 2204 | **2118 (1.04x)** |
| GPT-OSS 120B proxy, 8 of 36 layers | 852 | **821 (1.04x)** |

The 120B row uses the README's "120B tuning" settings. The 120B yaml (MBS 1) is unchanged: there only the
shared-expert GEMMs are tuned, about 0.6 ms of a 447 ms iteration.

lm loss and grad norms match the READMEs, with no NaN. The READMEs were measured on another MI455X node: the
baselines and GPT-OSS rows agree within 0.6%, while the FlyDSL rows differ by up to 3.5% between the two nodes
(DeepSeek-V3 faster on this one, Llama-3.1-8B slower).

Passing the tuning-file variable into Docker does not make the referenced host file available there: this launcher only mounts the repository. nodes.body: When running `PRIMUS_LAUNCHER=direct PRIMUS_HIPBLASLT_TUNING=1 PRIMUS_HIPBLASLT_TUNING_STAGE=3`, this unconditional default causes the tuning hook to select the bundled file instead of the result generated by stage 2. `prepare_experiment.sh:251` prefers any nonempty override, so re-tuning a different shape or hipBLASLt build is silently ignored. Suppress the bundled default during automatic tuning, as the DeepSeek and Llama launchers already do.

### 🟡 Changes recommended Custom Llama output workspaces outside the checkout are not mounted, so container removal can delete logs and profiler traces.
3 open issues - [External Primus workspace is not mounted for persistent output](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1312#discussion_r4375771041) · New - [Bundled tuning default overrides automatic stage 2 results](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1312#discussion_r4375729216) - [Host tuning override file is not mounted into Docker](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1312#discussion_r4375729158)
Review effort: Balanced

The documented `PRIMUS_WORKSPACE` setting is forwarded into the container, but only the repository is mounted for output. Setting it to a host directory outside the checkout, such as `/scratch/primus-output`, writes the logs and profiler traces into the container's private filesystem; `docker run --rm` then deletes them on exit. Please create and bind-mount the resolved workspace so custom output locations persist on the host.

+# Llama-3.1-8B on MI455X
+
+Llama-3.1-8B pretraining on MI455X (gfx1250): the full model (32 layers, hidden 4096, 32 query / 8 KV
+heads of dim 128), seq 8192, BF16, mock data, no activation recompute. Attention runs on Primus-Turbo's
+FlyDSL kernels and RMSNorm on Primus-Turbo. The config is
+`examples/megatron/configs/MI455X/llama3.1_8B-BF16-pretrain.yaml` and the launcher is
+`run_llama3.1_8b_mi455x.sh`: with `PRIMUS_LAUNCHER=container` (default) it starts a new container of
+`DOCKER_IMAGE` from the host and re-runs itself inside it; with `PRIMUS_LAUNCHER=direct` it runs inside
+the current container.
+
+The default image is `amdprimus/amdprimus:tas-20261019` (see the DeepSeek-V3 example's README). Its
+Primus-Turbo has no gfx1250 FlyDSL attention for head dim 128 (only the MLA one), so this example needs a
+Primus-Turbo checkout that has it (`primus_turbo/flydsl/attention/gfx1250/`, on `dev/mi455x_v2` since
+Primus-Turbo PR #574), passed as `TURBO_DIR`. The numbers below were measured with Primus-Turbo
+`dev/mi455x_v2` 85e85e70. With the backend left at `flydsl`, the launcher stops before training when the
+Primus-Turbo it would use lacks that directory.
+
+## Run
+
+Build the Primus-Turbo checkout in place for the image once (gfx1250 only, OpenMPI off the paths so
+rocSHMEM is not linked), then pass it as `TURBO_DIR`; the launcher puts it first on `PYTHONPATH`:
+
+```bash
+git clone https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus-Turbo.git /path/to/Primus-Turbo
+git -C /path/to/Primus-Turbo checkout 85e85e70  # dev/mi455x_v2 with PR #574, the commit measured below
+docker run --rm -u "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -e HOME=/tmp -v /path/to/Primus-Turbo:/path/to/Primus-Turbo \
+    -w /path/to/Primus-Turbo amdprimus/amdprimus:tas-20261019 bash -c \
+    'PATH=$(tr : "\n" <<< "$PATH" | grep -v openmpi | paste -sd:) GPU_ARCHS=gfx1250 python3 setup.py build_ext --inplace'
+
+# On the host, 4 GPUs (the default: GPUS_PER_NODE=4, DP4, GBS 16)
+TURBO_DIR=/path/to/Primus-Turbo bash examples/megatron/models/llama3.1-8b/run_llama3.1_8b_mi455x.sh
+
+# On the host, 1 GPU (GBS 4)
+GPUS_PER_NODE=1 TURBO_DIR=/path/to/Primus-Turbo bash examples/megatron/models/llama3.1-8b/run_llama3.1_8b_mi455x.sh
+
+# Inside a container (mount the Primus-Turbo checkout too); GPUS_PER_NODE works the same way
+PRIMUS_LAUNCHER=direct TURBO_DIR=/path/to/Primus-Turbo \
+    bash examples/megatron/models/llama3.1-8b/run_llama3.1_8b_mi455x.sh
+```
+
+**Settings** are environment variables:
+
+- Parallelism: `GPUS_PER_NODE` (default 4, data parallel), `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, `PRIMUS_TP`, `PRIMUS_PP`.
+- Training: `TRAIN_ITERS`, `MBS` (default 4), `GBS` (default `MBS` x `GPUS_PER_NODE`),
+  `PRIMUS_RECOMPUTE_LAYER_IDS` (layers to recompute, e.g. `0,3`; empty, the default, disables
+  recompute), `PRIMUS_SEQ_LENGTH` (default 8192) and `PRIMUS_MAX_POSITION_EMBEDDINGS` (default
+  `PRIMUS_SEQ_LENGTH`; Megatron needs it to be at least the sequence length).
+- Feature switches: `USE_TURBO_ATTENTION`, `USE_TURBO_RMS_NORM`, `MOCK_DATA`.
+- `PRIMUS_TURBO_ATTN_BACKEND`: `flydsl` (default) or `triton`, see Attention backends below.
+- `PROFILE=True` profiles iterations 6–7 (trace under `output/<team>/<user>/<exp>/tensorboard/`).
+- `PATCH_TRITON_EXPERT_SCHEDULING` (default `1`): see Triton expert scheduling below.
+- `HIPBLASLT_TUNING_OVERRIDE_FILE` (default: the file in `hipblaslt_tuning/`; empty: hipBLASLt's own
+  kernel choice): see hipBLASLt tuning below.
+- Config and output: `EXP` (the experiment yaml), and `PRIMUS_WORKSPACE` (default `output`), `PRIMUS_TEAM`,
+  `PRIMUS_USER`, `PRIMUS_EXP_NAME`, which make up the output directory `<workspace>/<team>/<user>/<exp>`.
+
+The defaults are in the script. Arguments to the script are appended to the Primus command line.
+
+If the Primus-Turbo checkout pins a FlyDSL version other than the image's, install it with
+`pip install --no-deps --target build/pydeps flydsl==<version>` in the checkout; `build/pydeps` is on the
+`PYTHONPATH` as well.
+
+**Output.** The console log is written to `output/<team>/<user>/<exp>/train.log`. From the host,
+training runs as root in the new container, so the files it creates are owned by root. Inside a
+container it runs as the container's user, which has to be root for the Triton patch.
+
+**Triton expert scheduling.** Triton 3.8 turns on AMDGPU expert scheduling for gfx1250, which makes
+Triton kernels (here the Inductor-compiled SwiGLU, and Primus-Turbo's Triton attention) fault or return
+NaN at random. The launcher sets
+`TRITON_HIP_USE_EXPERT_SCHEDULING=0`, which Triton applies whenever it compiles a kernel, and with
+`PATCH_TRITON_EXPERT_SCHEDULING=1` (the default) also makes `is_expert_scheduling_enabled()` in the
+container's Triton return `False`, which invalidates Inductor's cache of kernels compiled without the
+variable. The patch needs root and stays in a long-lived container; set
+`PATCH_TRITON_EXPERT_SCHEDULING=0` to skip it.
+
+**hipBLASLt tuning.** The launcher sets `HIPBLASLT_TUNING_OVERRIDE_FILE` to
+`hipblaslt_tuning/llama3.1_8b-gfx1250-hipblaslt_e1e7fdcab9-rocm_10.2.0a20261011.txt` (empty: hipBLASLt's own
+choice), which gives 11 of the 15 hipBLASLt GEMM shapes (4 x 8192 tokens per micro-batch) a faster kernel of
+hipBLASLt's library, e.g. FC1 forward 1.32x and the output layer forward 1.36x. Other hipBLASLt builds and
+shapes (another `MBS` x sequence length, or `PRIMUS_TP`) fall back to hipBLASLt's default. A file of your own
+may be given relative to the current directory; the launcher checks that it can be read and mounts it into
+the container. With Primus's own tuning flow (`PRIMUS_HIPBLASLT_TUNING=1`, see `examples/README.md`) the
+launcher sets no default, so its stage 3 uses the stage-2 result unless the variable is set. The file was made
+like the DeepSeek-V3 example's; see hipBLASLt tuning in its README.
+
+## Reference
+
+Measured with `amdprimus/amdprimus:tas-20261019` and Primus-Turbo 85e85e70, MBS 4 (one micro-batch of
+4 x 8192 tokens per GPU and iteration), started from the host. ms/iter is Primus's average over iterations
+3–10. The FlyDSL and hipBLASLt tuning rows are the mean of 2 runs that alternated between the two rows; the
+baseline rows are the mean of 3 runs from an earlier set, and the speedup is against them. Peak memory is
+the largest `hip mem usage` in the log, which Primus prints for the last rank in GiB (labelled GB) as the
+device's total minus free memory. Each row adds one step:

+- FlyDSL: Primus-Turbo's FlyDSL attention.
+- hipBLASLt tuning: the tuning file above. This row is the launcher's defaults.

+TE's unfused attention (`USE_TURBO_ATTENTION=False`) is not in the tables: without recompute it runs out of

+are not fully hidden), and the distributed optimizer's sharding lowers the peak memory per GPU by about
+69 GiB. The loss differs between 1 and 4 GPUs because the global batch does (4 vs 16 sequences). Without the
+tuning file, `PRIMUS_SEQ_LENGTH=16384` with `MBS=2` (the same tokens per iteration) ran 1231 ms/iter on one
+GPU.
+
+From the host every run starts a new container and takes about 60 s from launch to exit on 1 or 4 GPUs
+(the Triton patch invalidates Inductor's cache, and the FlyDSL kernels are compiled once); a repeat run on
+one GPU in a long-lived container takes about 40 s.
+
+Attention alone at this shape (b 4, seq 8192, 32/8 heads, causal; mean of 100 calls after 20 warmups):
+
+| Attention | Forward ms | Backward ms |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Primus-Turbo FlyDSL | 1.19 | 4.01 |
+| Primus-Turbo Triton | 4.99 | 25.58 |
+| TE unfused | 44.36 | 41.66 |
+
+## Known issues
+
+- **Attention backends.** The FlyDSL kernels (the default, `PRIMUS_TURBO_ATTN_BACKEND=flydsl`) take BF16
+  attention with head dim 128, 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16 query heads per KV head, query lengths that are
+  multiples of 64, KV lengths that are multiples of 32, no dropout, bias or sliding window, and q and k
+  tensors of at most 1 GiB each (`MBS` <= 16 at seq 8192 with 32 heads per GPU); with the backend set to
+  `flydsl`, any other call raises `ValueError`. The fused backward measured here needs causal attention,
+  query lengths that are multiples of 64 and KV lengths that are multiples of 128; other calls use the
+  deterministic two-kernel backward. With a
+  Primus-Turbo that lacks `primus_turbo/flydsl/attention/gfx1250/` (e.g. the image's own), every call
+  raises that `ValueError`. Primus-Turbo's Triton attention (`PRIMUS_TURBO_ATTN_BACKEND=triton`) needs
+  Triton's expert scheduling off (see Triton expert scheduling above): with it on, the Triton attention
+  forward made illegal memory accesses or gave NaN at this shape. `USE_TURBO_ATTENTION=False` runs TE's
+  `DotProductAttention`, not PyTorch SDPA. On gfx1250 TE has neither of its fused attention backends for
+  this input, and the image has no `flash_attn` package, so TE uses `UnfusedDotProductAttention`. That
+  keeps the 8192 x 8192 attention probabilities of every layer for the backward pass, and at `MBS` 4 the
+  first iteration runs out of memory; `--recompute_granularity selective` (recompute the core attention
+  in the backward pass) makes it fit.
+- **Determinism.** The fused FlyDSL backward adds dQ with atomics, so dQ (and from there the loss) can
+  differ between runs in the last bits (lm loss 10.1902 and 10.1903 at iteration 10 in the 1-GPU table); dK
+  and dV are reproducible. Primus passes Megatron's `deterministic_mode` to Primus-Turbo, which then runs
+  the deterministic two-kernel backward instead. Megatron's deterministic mode is not set up by this example
+  and was not measured: it needs `--deterministic_mode True --cross_entropy_loss_fusion False`, `NCCL_ALGO`
+  set to one of Megatron's all-reduce algorithms (e.g. `Ring`), and, checked by Primus on ROCm,
+  `PRIMUS_DETERMINISTIC=1`, `TORCH_COMPILE_DISABLE=1` (which also turns off the compiled SwiGLU),
+  `ROCBLAS_DEFAULT_ATOMICS_MODE=0` and `PRIMUS_TURBO_AUTO_TUNE=0`.

+#!/bin/bash
+###############################################################################
+# Copyright (c) 2026, Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. All rights reserved.
+#
+# See LICENSE for license information.
+###############################################################################
+#
+# Llama-3.1-8B pretraining on one MI455X node.
+#
+#   TURBO_DIR=/path/to/Primus-Turbo bash examples/megatron/models/llama3.1-8b/run_llama3.1_8b_mi455x.sh  # on the host
+#   PRIMUS_LAUNCHER=direct TURBO_DIR=... bash examples/megatron/models/llama3.1-8b/run_llama3.1_8b_mi455x.sh  # in a container
+#
+# Settings are the environment variables below. Extra arguments are appended
+# to the Primus command line.
+###############################################################################
+set -euo pipefail
+
+SCRIPT=$(realpath "$0")
+# relative to the caller's directory
+if [[ -n "${TURBO_DIR:-}" ]]; then
+    TURBO_DIR=$(realpath -e "${TURBO_DIR}")
+fi
+if [[ -n "${HIPBLASLT_TUNING_OVERRIDE_FILE:-}" ]]; then
+    HIPBLASLT_TUNING_OVERRIDE_FILE=$(realpath -e "${HIPBLASLT_TUNING_OVERRIDE_FILE}")
+fi
+cd "$(dirname "${SCRIPT}")/../../../.."
+
+# container: re-run this script in a new container of DOCKER_IMAGE; direct: run in this container
+export PRIMUS_LAUNCHER=${PRIMUS_LAUNCHER:-container}
+export DOCKER_IMAGE=${DOCKER_IMAGE:-amdprimus/amdprimus:tas-20261019}
+export EXP=${EXP:-examples/megatron/configs/MI455X/llama3.1_8B-BF16-pretrain.yaml}
+# Primus-Turbo checkout built in place for DOCKER_IMAGE (see README.md); empty: the image's primus_turbo
+export TURBO_DIR=${TURBO_DIR:-}
+
+export GPUS_PER_NODE=${GPUS_PER_NODE:-4}
+export HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=${HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES:-$(seq -s, 0 $((GPUS_PER_NODE - 1)))}
+export TRAIN_ITERS=${TRAIN_ITERS:-10}
+export MBS=${MBS:-4}
+export GBS=${GBS:-$((MBS * GPUS_PER_NODE))}
+export PRIMUS_TP=${PRIMUS_TP:-1}
+export PRIMUS_PP=${PRIMUS_PP:-1}
+# max_position_embeddings follows the sequence length unless set: Megatron needs it >= seq_length
+export PRIMUS_SEQ_LENGTH=${PRIMUS_SEQ_LENGTH:-8192}
+export PRIMUS_MAX_POSITION_EMBEDDINGS=${PRIMUS_MAX_POSITION_EMBEDDINGS:-${PRIMUS_SEQ_LENGTH}}
+# layers to recompute in full, e.g. 0,3; empty: no recompute
+export PRIMUS_RECOMPUTE_LAYER_IDS=${PRIMUS_RECOMPUTE_LAYER_IDS:-}
+export USE_TURBO_ATTENTION=${USE_TURBO_ATTENTION:-True}
+export USE_TURBO_RMS_NORM=${USE_TURBO_RMS_NORM:-True}
+# Primus-Turbo attention backend: flydsl (needs the gfx1250 head-dim-128 kernels, see README.md)
+# or triton
+export PRIMUS_TURBO_ATTN_BACKEND=${PRIMUS_TURBO_ATTN_BACKEND:-flydsl}
+case "${PRIMUS_TURBO_ATTN_BACKEND,,}" in
+    flydsl | triton) ;;
+    *)
+        echo "PRIMUS_TURBO_ATTN_BACKEND must be flydsl or triton, not '${PRIMUS_TURBO_ATTN_BACKEND}'" >&2
+        exit 2
+        ;;
+esac
+export MOCK_DATA=${MOCK_DATA:-True}
+export PROFILE=${PROFILE:-False}
+# 1: switch Triton's gfx1250 expert scheduling off in the container's Triton (needs root), see below
+export PATCH_TRITON_EXPERT_SCHEDULING=${PATCH_TRITON_EXPERT_SCHEDULING:-1}
+# hipBLASLt kernels tuned for this example's GEMMs (README.md); empty: hipBLASLt's own choice. hipBLASLt
+# uses a row only while its solution index still names the kernel it was tuned with. No default with
+# PRIMUS_HIPBLASLT_TUNING=1: its stage 3 would take this file instead of the stage-2 result.
+if [[ "${PRIMUS_HIPBLASLT_TUNING:-0}" == 1 ]]; then
+    export HIPBLASLT_TUNING_OVERRIDE_FILE=${HIPBLASLT_TUNING_OVERRIDE_FILE-}
+else
+    export HIPBLASLT_TUNING_OVERRIDE_FILE=${HIPBLASLT_TUNING_OVERRIDE_FILE-$(dirname "${SCRIPT}")/hipblaslt_tuning/llama3.1_8b-gfx1250-hipblaslt_e1e7fdcab9-rocm_10.2.0a20261011.txt}
+fi
+if [[ -n "${HIPBLASLT_TUNING_OVERRIDE_FILE}" && ! -r "${HIPBLASLT_TUNING_OVERRIDE_FILE}" ]]; then
+    echo "cannot read HIPBLASLT_TUNING_OVERRIDE_FILE=${HIPBLASLT_TUNING_OVERRIDE_FILE}" >&2
+    exit 2
+fi
+
+export PRIMUS_TEAM=${PRIMUS_TEAM:-amd}
+export PRIMUS_USER=${PRIMUS_USER:-$(id -un)}
+export PRIMUS_EXP_NAME=${PRIMUS_EXP_NAME:-llama3.1_8b_${GPUS_PER_NODE}gpu_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)}
+
+case "${PRIMUS_LAUNCHER}" in
+    container)
+        # The settings above, plus the single-node variables `primus-cli container` passes through
+        ENV_ARGS=(-e PRIMUS_LAUNCHER=direct)
+        while IFS= read -r v; do
+            case "${v}" in
+                PRIMUS_LAUNCHER) ;;
+                EXP | TURBO_DIR | GPUS_PER_NODE | HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES | TRAIN_ITERS | MBS | GBS | USE_TURBO_* | \
+                    MOCK_DATA | PROFILE | PATCH_TRITON_EXPERT_SCHEDULING | \
+                    MASTER_ADDR | MASTER_PORT | HF_TOKEN | WANDB_API_KEY | ENABLE_NUMA_BINDING | GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES | \
+                    HSA_* | NVTE_* | PRIMUS_* | NCCL_* | RCCL_* | GLOO_* | IONIC_* | HIPBLASLT_*)
+                    ENV_ARGS+=(-e "${v}")
+                    ;;
+            esac
+        done < <(compgen -e)
+        DOCKER_ARGS=(--device /dev/kfd --device /dev/dri -v "${PWD}:${PWD}")
+        if [[ -e /dev/infiniband ]]; then
+            DOCKER_ARGS+=(--device /dev/infiniband)
+        fi
+        if [[ -n "${TURBO_DIR}" ]]; then
+            DOCKER_ARGS+=(-v "${TURBO_DIR}:${TURBO_DIR}")
+        fi
+        if [[ -n "${HIPBLASLT_TUNING_OVERRIDE_FILE}" ]]; then
+            DOCKER_ARGS+=(-v "${HIPBLASLT_TUNING_OVERRIDE_FILE}:${HIPBLASLT_TUNING_OVERRIDE_FILE}:ro")
+        fi
+        # Same runtime options as `primus-cli container` (runner/.primus.yaml)
+        exec docker run --rm --name "llama3.1-8b-mi455x-$$" \
+            --ipc host --network host --privileged --group-add video \
+            --cap-add SYS_PTRACE --cap-add CAP_SYS_ADMIN --security-opt seccomp=unconfined \
+            --ulimit nofile=1048576:1048576 "${DOCKER_ARGS[@]}" -w "${PWD}" "${ENV_ARGS[@]}" \
+            "${DOCKER_IMAGE}" bash "${SCRIPT}" "$@"
+        ;;
+    direct) ;;
+    *)
+        echo "PRIMUS_LAUNCHER must be container or direct, not '${PRIMUS_LAUNCHER}'" >&2
+        exit 2
+        ;;
+esac
+
+# The flydsl backend needs Primus-Turbo's gfx1250 head-dim-128 kernels (README.md). Without them the
+# first attention call raises ValueError, after the model and optimizer are built; stop here instead.
+if [[ "${USE_TURBO_ATTENTION,,}" =~ ^(true|1|yes)$ && "${PRIMUS_TURBO_ATTN_BACKEND,,}" == flydsl ]]; then
+    if [[ -n "${TURBO_DIR}" ]]; then
+        TURBO_PKG=${TURBO_DIR}/primus_turbo
+    else
+        TURBO_PKG=$(python3 -c 'import importlib.util, os; s = importlib.util.find_spec("primus_turbo"); print(os.path.dirname(s.origin) if s and s.origin else "")')
+    fi
+    if [[ ! -d "${TURBO_PKG}/flydsl/attention/gfx1250" ]]; then
+        echo "PRIMUS_TURBO_ATTN_BACKEND=flydsl needs a Primus-Turbo with primus_turbo/flydsl/attention/gfx1250/," \
+            "which ${TURBO_PKG:-this Python environment} lacks. Set TURBO_DIR to such a checkout (README.md)" \
+            "or PRIMUS_TURBO_ATTN_BACKEND=triton." >&2
+        exit 2
+    fi
+fi
+
+# Triton 3.8 turns on AMDGPU expert scheduling for gfx1250, which makes Triton kernels fault or
+# return NaN at random. TRITON_HIP_USE_EXPERT_SCHEDULING=0 (below) turns it off when a kernel is
+# compiled, but Inductor loads kernels from its own cache without compiling them; changing Triton's
+# default also invalidates that cache.
+if [[ "${PATCH_TRITON_EXPERT_SCHEDULING}" == 1 ]]; then
+    TRITON_AMD_COMPILER=$(python3 -c 'import os, triton; print(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(triton.__file__), "backends", "amd", "compiler.py"))')
+    if ! grep -q '^def is_expert_scheduling_enabled(arch):' "${TRITON_AMD_COMPILER}"; then
+        echo "no is_expert_scheduling_enabled(arch) in ${TRITON_AMD_COMPILER}; Triton not patched" >&2
+    elif ! grep -A1 '^def is_expert_scheduling_enabled(arch):' "${TRITON_AMD_COMPILER}" | grep -q '^    return False$'; then
+        if [[ ! -w "$(dirname "${TRITON_AMD_COMPILER}")" ]]; then
+            echo "cannot patch ${TRITON_AMD_COMPILER} as uid $(id -u); run as root or set PATCH_TRITON_EXPERT_SCHEDULING=0" >&2
+            exit 2
+        fi
+        sed -i '/^def is_expert_scheduling_enabled(arch):/a\    return False' "${TRITON_AMD_COMPILER}"
+        echo "patched ${TRITON_AMD_COMPILER}: is_expert_scheduling_enabled() -> False"
+    fi
+fi
+
+# hipBLASLt takes a set but empty HIPBLASLT_TUNING_OVERRIDE_FILE as an override file named ""
+if [[ -z "${HIPBLASLT_TUNING_OVERRIDE_FILE}" ]]; then
+    unset HIPBLASLT_TUNING_OVERRIDE_FILE
+fi
+
+ENV_ARGS=(
+    --env PRIMUS_GPU_MODEL=MI455X
+    --env NNODES=1
+    --env GPUS_PER_NODE="${GPUS_PER_NODE}"
+    --env HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES="${HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES}"
+    --env TRITON_HIP_USE_EXPERT_SCHEDULING=0
+    --env PRIMUS_TURBO_ATTN_BACKEND="${PRIMUS_TURBO_ATTN_BACKEND}"
+    --env HSA_COREDUMP_PATTERN=/dev/null
+)
+if [[ -n "${TURBO_DIR}" ]]; then
+    # --env is applied after Primus builds PYTHONPATH, so this checkout comes first.
+    ENV_ARGS+=(
+        --env "PYTHONPATH=${TURBO_DIR}:${TURBO_DIR}/build/pydeps:${PWD}:${PWD}/third_party/Megatron-LM"
+        --env PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
+    )
+fi
+
+if [[ -n "${PRIMUS_RECOMPUTE_LAYER_IDS}" ]]; then
+    # as a list: Primus reads a single id as an int
+    RECOMPUTE_ARGS=(--recompute_granularity full --recompute_layer_ids "[${PRIMUS_RECOMPUTE_LAYER_IDS//[][]/}]")
+else
+    RECOMPUTE_ARGS=(--recompute_granularity null --recompute_layer_ids null)
+fi
+
+LOG_DIR="${PRIMUS_WORKSPACE:-output}/${PRIMUS_TEAM}/${PRIMUS_USER}/${PRIMUS_EXP_NAME}"
+mkdir -p "${LOG_DIR}"
+./primus-cli direct "${ENV_ARGS[@]}" -- train pretrain --config "${EXP}" \
+    --train_iters "${TRAIN_ITERS}" \
+    --micro_batch_size "${MBS}" \
+    --global_batch_size "${GBS}" \
+    --tensor_model_parallel_size "${PRIMUS_TP}" \
+    --pipeline_model_parallel_size "${PRIMUS_PP}" \
+    "${RECOMPUTE_ARGS[@]}" \
+    --use_turbo_attention "${USE_TURBO_ATTENTION}" \
+    --use_turbo_rms_norm "${USE_TURBO_RMS_NORM}" \
+    --mock_data "${MOCK_DATA}" \
+    --profile "${PROFILE}" \
+    --use_pytorch_profiler "${PROFILE}" \
+    --profile_step_start 6 \
+    --profile_step_end 8 \
+    "$@" 2>&1 | tee "${LOG_DIR}/train.log"

The documented `PRIMUS_WORKSPACE` setting is forwarded into the container, but only the repository is mounted for output. Setting it to a host directory outside the checkout, such as `/scratch/primus-output`, writes the logs and profiler traces into the container's private filesystem; `docker run --rm` then deletes them on exit.
